parse.text:
Catalan

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From des- +‎ vestir.

Verb

[edit]

desvestir (first-person singular present desvesteixo, first-person singular preterite desvestí, past participle desvestit)

  1. (transitive, reflexive) to undress
    Synonym: despullar

Further reading

[edit]
  • “desvestir”, in Gran Diccionari de la Llengua Catalana, Grup Enciclopèdia Catalana, 2026

Old French

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From des- +‎ vestir.

Verb

[edit]

desvestir

  1. (transitive) to undress
    • c. 1170, Chrétien de Troyes, Érec et Énide:
      Son seignor desarme et desvest
      She disarmed and undressed him
  2. (reflexive, se desvestir) to get undressed

Spanish

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From des- +‎ vestir, or from Latin disvestīre.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /desbesˈtiɾ/ [d̪ez.β̞esˈt̪iɾ]
  • Audio (Colombia):(file)
  • Rhymes: -iɾ
  • Syllabification: des‧ves‧tir

Verb

[edit]

desvestir (first-person singular present desvisto, first-person singular preterite desvestí, past participle desvestido)

  1. (transitive) to undress (another)
    Synonym: desnudar
  2. (reflexive) to undress (oneself)
    Synonym: desnudarse
